frames.narration: 12 vectors are stored in three lists, one for each centroid. A query arrives. Exact search would compute 12 distances.
The query is compared with the three centroids first. B is closest, then A, then C.
Probing one list (B) computes 4 distances and returns p4, at distance 1.204. Fast, but the true nearest is not there.
The true nearest neighbour, p2, sits at 0.906, in list A, across the cell boundary. One probe missed it.
Probing two lists (B and A) computes 8 distances and finds p2. More probes buy recall at the price of more work.
To fit in memory, product quantization can store each vector as a short code, such as 16 bytes instead of 512, and estimate distances from the codes.
